tagline: From sagebrush to aspens, a mountain loop above the Alvord Desert
intro: The Steens Loop Tour Route climbs from Frenchglen toward the top of Steens Mountain on a 59-mile circuit. Oregon’s transportation department presents the tour route in its scenic-byways program, highlighting wildlife, glaciated canyons and changing plant communities. It gives a minimum driving time of three to five hours. Steens is a fault-block mountain, its eastern edge pushed upward along a fault. From the east rim overlook, the mountain drops more than a vertical mile to the Alvord Desert floor.

The upper mountain’s meadows once drew cattlemen and Irish and Basque sheepherders for summer grazing. At Whorehouse Meadow, aspen carvings left by Basque American sheepherders remain, while the maps record a later dispute: the Bureau of Land Management replaced the name with Naughty Girl Meadow in the 1960s, then restored it in 1981 after public outcry.

From Frenchglen, the climb passes from sagebrush into juniper, then quaking aspen and mountain mahogany as moisture increases. Kiger Gorge’s overlook reaches the headwall of a U-shaped canyon; the east rim overlooks a drop of more than a vertical mile to the Alvord Desert. The loop finishes through the range of the South Steens Wild Horse Herd, managed by the Bureau of Land Management.

moments.title: Frenchglen
moments.text: Frenchglen takes its name from the French-Glenn Livestock Company, whose headquarters were established here in 1872. The post office adopted the name after moving here. The historic Frenchglen Hotel sits at the northern end of the mountain loop. Its early guests had business at P Ranch or came to visit Malheur National Wildlife Refuge. Civilian Conservation Corps labor helped restore and enlarge the hotel in 1937–38; Oregon’s parks department took possession in 1973. The historic building has eight guest rooms, with additional accommodation in the modern Drovers’ Inn. Guests continue to visit for the refuge and Steens Mountain.

moments.title: Whorehouse Meadow
moments.text: Aspens surrounding Whorehouse Meadow retain carvings made by Basque American sheepherders, some of them explicit. The meadow lies on Steens Mountain’s western slope within the Steens Mountain Wilderness. Women from Vale once set up wood-and-canvas tents here to serve the area’s sheepherders and cattlemen. The name itself became a cartographic dispute. Bureau of Land Management maps changed it to Naughty Girl Meadow in the 1960s; public outcry brought Whorehouse Meadow back in 1981. In Oregon Geographic Names, Lewis McArthur places it a mile east of Fish Lake, describing a meadow both accessible and secluded.

moments.title: Kiger Gorge
moments.text: Kiger Gorge’s overlook stands at the headwall of a U-shaped canyon, one of five major glaciated canyons on Steens Mountain. The mountain itself formed when pressure pushed its eastern edge upward along a fault. Ice later carved deep gorges and left depressions now occupied by Lily, Fish and Wildhorse lakes.
moments.notice: The canyon’s U-shaped profile records glacial carving.

practical: Kiger Gorge: The loop road closes in winter; ODOT gives July through October as the best time to visit. (checked 2026-10-11)
